title: I have
goal: Use the verb لرل (to have) and set up the six present-tense verb endings — endings you will use in every sentence from this unit to the last page.
bekal: say what you have and don't have
use the six present-tense verb endings
negate sentences with نه in front of the verb

dialogs.title: خبرې اترې — د چای په دکان کې
dialogs.intro: Late afternoon at a teahouse near the house. Ahmad, Najib's brother, sits with Budi while they wait for their green tea.

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: بودي، تاسو په کابل کې ملګري لرئ؟
lines.baca: Būdī, tāso pə Kābəl ke malgərī larəy?
lines.id: Budi, do you have friends in Kabul?
lines.literal: Budi, you(pl) in Kabul in friends have-you(pl)?

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Now I have one friend — you!

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: ښه ځواب دی. زه ډېر ملګري لرم، خو وخت نه لرم.
lines.baca: ṣa dzawāb day. zə ḍer malgərī larəm, kho wakht nə larəm.
lines.id: Good answer. I have lots of friends, but no time.
lines.literal: good answer is. I many friends have-I, but time not have-I.

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: زه په پوهنتون کې لولم او په دکان کې کار کوم.
lines.baca: zə pə pohantūn ke lwaləm aw pə dūkān ke kār kawəm.
lines.id: I study at the university and work in a shop.
lines.literal: I at university in read-I and in shop in work do-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: What kind of shop do you have?

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: زمونږ کورنۍ د مېوو دکان لري. زه هلته مرسته کوم.
lines.baca: zmūẓ kornəy də mewo dūkān larī. zə halta marasta kawəm.
lines.id: Our family has a fruit shop. I help out there.
lines.literal: of-us family of fruits shop has-it. I there help do-I.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: زه هم کار غواړم، خو زه پښتو ښه نه وایم.
lines.baca: zə ham kār ghwāṛəm, kho zə paṣto ṣa nə wāyəm.
lines.id: I'd like to work too, but I don't speak Pashto well yet.
lines.literal: I also work want-I, but I Pashto well not say-I.

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: تاسو ښه وایئ! ډېر ښه وایئ.
lines.baca: tāso ṣa wāyəy! ḍer ṣa wāyəy.
lines.literal: you(pl) well say-you(pl)! very well say-you(pl).

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.text: مننه، خو زه ډېرې کلمې نه پوهېږم.
lines.baca: manana, kho zə ḍere kalime nə poheẓəm.
lines.id: Thanks, but there are lots of words I don't understand.
lines.literal: thanks, but I many words not understand-I.

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: هېڅ پروا نه لري. مونږ وخت لرو.
lines.baca: hets parwā nə larī. mūẓ wakht larū.
lines.literal: at-all care not has-it. we time have-we.

lines.speaker: بودي:
lines.id: Do you have brothers and sisters?

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: هو، دوه ورونه او یوه خور لرم. نجیب زما مشر ورور دی.
lines.baca: ho, dwa wrūṇa aw yawa khor larəm. Najīb zmā məshr wror day.
lines.id: Yes, I have two brothers and one sister. Najib is my older brother.
lines.literal: yes, two brothers and one sister have-I. Najib of-me big brother is.

lines.speaker: احمد:
lines.text: نه، زه واده نه لرم. لا محصل یم!
lines.baca: nə, zə wāda nə larəm. lā mahsal yəm!
lines.id: No, I'm not married. I'm still a student!
lines.literal: no, I marriage not have-I. still student am-I!

notes: The verb لرل is Pashto's biggest gift to English speakers. Persian, Urdu, Arabic, and Hebrew all go the long way round to say "I have"; Pashto uses an ordinary verb, just like English. The sentence is زه یو کتاب لرم, literally "I one book have" — only the verb moves to the end.

Notice that the ending ـم appears on many verbs at once: لرم، کوم، وایم، غواړم، پوهېږم. That ending is what means "I". Once the six endings in the grammar box stick, you can use any verb you come across.

The phrase هېڅ پروا نه لري literally means "it has no care at all", and it means "no problem". It is the standard reply both to an apology and to a thank-you, and you will hear it dozens of times a day.
The word خو means "but" and goes at the start of its clause, just like English. There is also مګر *magar* with the same meaning, a little more formal and a little more Persian.

Look at the order of نه and its verb once more. The sentence وخت **نه** لرم is right; وخت لرم **نه** is wrong. The word نه always goes right before the verb, never after it, and never at the start of the sentence.

The word مشر means "older" and کشر means "younger". Pashto distinguishes an older brother from a younger one, which English does not do with a single word — and Afghans will be pleased if you get it right.

grammars.title: The six present-tense endings
body: Pashto verbs need no helper word in the present tense. Only the ending changes, and the endings are the same for almost every verb — this is what makes Pashto much lighter than it looks.
Notice that the forms for "he/she" and for "they" are exactly the same: ـي. Pashto does not distinguish them in the present tense, so that is one form you can forget about.

grammars.title: Negating with نه
body: Negating a Pashto sentence takes just one word in one place: نه, right before the verb. No verb form changes, no helper word appears, nothing is rearranged.
⚠️ One thing to watch: for **prohibitions**, use مه, not نه. The sentence مه ځه means "don't go"; نه ځه means nothing. Commands are covered fully in unit 16.

sections.title: Jobs, belongings, and your first verbs

blocks.title: Verbs whose "I" form can't be guessed
items: Most Pashto verbs behave neatly: لرل becomes لرم · کول becomes کوم. But the most common verbs are the ones that change shape, and there is no point fighting it — learn their "I" form as a new word.

Examples you need from now on: تلل (to go) becomes **ځم** · راتلل (to come) becomes **راځم** · لیدل (to see) becomes **وینم** · خوړل (to eat) becomes **خورم** · غوښتل (to want) becomes **غواړم** · لوستل (to read) becomes **لولم**.
Notice that the ending is still ـم as usual. Only the body of the word changes, and once you know that body, the other five forms follow the same rule.
The back of this book lists the fifty most common verbs with their "I" form. Don't memorize them all at once; use the list for looking things up.

blocks.title: Asking about what people have
items: For things: تاسو موټر لرئ؟ *tāso moṭar larəy* — "do you have a car?". The answer is هو، لرم or نه، نه لرم.
For people: تاسو ماشومان لرئ؟ *tāso māshūmān larəy* — "do you have children?". This is a very ordinary question in Afghanistan and not considered too personal at all.
For situations: زه وخت نه لرم *zə wakht nə larəm* — "I don't have time". The most polite and most common way of saying no.
⚠️ Pashto uses لرل for things English says with "there is": غر واوره لري, literally "the mountain has snow", meaning "there is snow on the mountain".

exercises.prompt: Complete with the right form of لرل.
Put the words in the right order.
items: کوم / زه / کار / کې / دکان / په

answers: زه یو ملګری لرم. — مونږ وخت نه لرو. — تاسو موټر لرئ؟ — هغه په دکان کې کار کوي. — زه نه پوهېږم.
زه وخت نه لرم. — هغه کار نه کوي. — مونږ نه پوهېږو. — تاسو پښتو نه وایئ. — دا زما کتاب نه دی.
